169	// Inclut toujours "default" (thème intégré) + les fichiers JSON du répertoire themes
170	func ListThemes() ([]string, error) {
171		themes := []string{"default"}
172	
173		dir, err := ThemeDir()
174		if err != nil {
175			return themes, nil // Retourner au moins "dark"
176		}
177	
178		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
179		if err != nil {
180			return themes, nil // Répertoire n'existe pas encore
181		}
182	
183		for _, entry := range entries {
184			if entry.IsDir() {
185				continue
186			}
187			name := entry.Name()
188			if themeName, ok := strings.CutSuffix(name, ".json"); ok {
189				// Éviter le doublon avec le thème intégré
190				if themeName == "default" {
191					continue
192				}
193				themes = append(themes, themeName)
194			}
195		}

197		return themes, nil

201	func applyColor(hex string, fallback lipgloss.Color) lipgloss.Color {
202		if hex == "" {
203			return fallback
204		}
205		return lipgloss.Color(hex)

208	// ApplyTheme applique un thème en mettant à jour les variables de couleur globales
209	// puis en rafraîchissant tous les styles
210	func ApplyTheme(t *Theme) {
211		// Mettre à jour les couleurs sémantiques globales
212		ColorOK = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorOK)
213		ColorError = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorError)
214		ColorWarn = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorWarn)
215	
216		ColorPrimary = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorPrimary)
217		ColorSecondary = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorSecondary)
218		ColorBorder = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorBorder)
219		ColorText = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorText)
220		ColorDim = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorDim)
221		ColorHighlight = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorHighlight)
222		ColorWhite = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorWhite)
223		ColorBlack = lipgloss.Color(t.ColorBlack)
224		ColorBackground = applyColor(t.ColorBackground, ColorBackground)
225	
226		// Appliquer les couleurs par composant (fallback sur couleurs sémantiques)
227		ColorTitleFg = applyColor(t.TitleFg, ColorPrimary)
228		ColorAppTitleFg = applyColor(t.AppTitleFg, ColorPrimary)
229		ColorSubTitleFg = applyColor(t.SubTitleFg, ColorSecondary)
230	
231		ColorButtonFg = applyColor(t.ButtonFg, ColorWhite)
232		ColorButtonBg = applyColor(t.ButtonBg, ColorPrimary)
233		ColorButtonInactiveFg = applyColor(t.ButtonInactiveFg, ColorWhite)
234		ColorButtonInactiveBg = applyColor(t.ButtonInactiveBg, ColorDim)
235	
236		ColorTabActiveFg = applyColor(t.TabActiveFg, ColorBlack)
237		ColorTabActiveBg = applyColor(t.TabActiveBg, ColorSecondary)
238		ColorTabInactiveFg = applyColor(t.TabInactiveFg, ColorDim)
239		ColorTabInactiveBg = applyColor(t.TabInactiveBg, ColorCmdLineBg)
240	
241		ColorTableHeaderFg = applyColor(t.TableHeaderFg, ColorSecondary)
242		ColorTableSelectedFg = applyColor(t.TableSelectedFg, ColorBlack)
243		ColorTableSelectedBg = applyColor(t.TableSelectedBg, ColorSecondary)
244	
245		ColorCmdLineFg = applyColor(t.CmdLineFg, ColorHighlight)
246		ColorCmdLineBg = applyColor(t.CmdLineBg, ColorCmdLineBg)
247	
248		// Le fond d'un graphe est celui de la ligne de commande : c'est la surface
249		// « un cran plus claire » que chaque thème définit déjà, donc un graphe se
250		// détache du reste de sa boîte sans qu'aucun thème ait à déclarer une
251		// couleur de plus.
252		ColorChartBg = ColorCmdLineBg
253		ColorCmdLineInactiveFg = applyColor(t.CmdLineInactiveFg, ColorDim)
254	
255		ColorViewportBorder = applyColor(t.ViewportBorder, ColorBorder)
256	
257		ColorHeaderKey = ColorSecondary
258	
259		// Syntax colors: aliases of the semantic palette, assigned here rather than
260		// at declaration because the palette itself is only populated by this
261		// function — a package-level `= ColorSecondary` would capture the zero
262		// value and never follow a theme change. ColorChartBg above is the same
263		// pattern.
264		ColorSyntaxKey = ColorSecondary
265		ColorSyntaxString = ColorOK
266		ColorSyntaxNumber = ColorHighlight
267		ColorSyntaxLiteral = ColorPrimary
268		ColorSyntaxPunct = ColorDim
269		ColorSyntaxTag = ColorSecondary
270		ColorSyntaxAttr = ColorPrimary
271		ColorSyntaxComment = ColorDim
272	
273		// A keyword shares the literal's colour today, and that is deliberate
274		// rather than an oversight: `if` and `true` are both words of the language,
275		// so the pairing is defensible until a theme decides otherwise — at which
276		// point it has a name to decide about. It is the argument already made for
277		// ColorFooterError against ColorError.
278		ColorSyntaxKeyword = ColorPrimary
279	
280		// A heading takes the key colour, and its weight comes from the style
281		// rather than from here.
282		ColorSyntaxHeading = ColorSecondary
283	
284		ColorSearchMatch = ColorHighlight
285		ColorSearchMatchFg = ColorBlack
286	
287		// Severity colors (background + foreground pairs)
288		ColorSeverityCritical = applyColor(t.SeverityCritical, ColorError)
289		ColorSeverityCriticalFg = applyColor(t.SeverityCriticalFg, ColorBlack)
290		ColorSeverityHigh = applyColor(t.SeverityHigh, ColorSeverityHigh)
291		ColorSeverityHighFg = applyColor(t.SeverityHighFg, ColorBlack)
292		ColorSeverityMedium = applyColor(t.SeverityMedium, ColorWarn)
293		ColorSeverityMediumFg = applyColor(t.SeverityMediumFg, ColorBlack)
294		ColorSeverityLow = applyColor(t.SeverityLow, ColorCmdLineBg)
295		ColorSeverityLowFg = applyColor(t.SeverityLowFg, ColorText)
296		ColorSeverityInfo = applyColor(t.SeverityInfo, ColorSeverityInfo)
297		ColorSeverityInfoFg = applyColor(t.SeverityInfoFg, ColorText)
298	
299		// Footer message colours (Rule 128). Assigned after the severity block
300		// because they alias it — the intent is that a footer error reads like a
301		// CRITICAL finding and a warning like a MEDIUM one.
302		ColorFooterInfo = ColorText
303		ColorFooterWarn = ColorSeverityMedium
304		ColorFooterError = ColorSeverityCritical
305	
306		// Icon colours (iconcolors.go). Assigned here like every other alias, and
307		// through applyColor so a theme file can name its own.
308		//
309		// The defaults carry an argument each. A namespace takes the structural
310		// colour the headers and tabs already use, and a repository the leaf colour
311		// beside it. Public is green because it is the state worth spotting without
312		// reading; internal is the warning hue because it is restricted without being
313		// closed; and private is **dim** because it is the majority — a colour every
314		// row carries informs of nothing (Rule 122), which is the same argument the
315		// severity counters make for their zeroes.
316		ColorIconNamespace = applyColor(t.IconNamespace, ColorSecondary)
317		ColorIconRepository = applyColor(t.IconRepository, ColorPrimary)
318		ColorIconVisPublic = applyColor(t.IconVisPublic, ColorOK)
319		ColorIconVisInternal = applyColor(t.IconVisInternal, ColorWarn)
320		ColorIconVisPrivate = applyColor(t.IconVisPrivate, ColorDim)
321	
322		// The workspaces and :sec listings. A directory takes the namespace's
323		// colour and the argument is the same shape: both are the thing that
324		// *holds* repositories, on a forge and on a disk. They are two roles rather
325		// than one alias so a theme can separate them; the default says they are
326		// the same idea.
327		ColorIconDirectory = applyColor(t.IconDirectory, ColorSecondary)
328	
329		// A loose file in a workspaces listing is the row nothing applies to — W, S
330		// and F are all greyed for it (Rule 130, availability.go). Dim is what the
331		// shortcut column already says about that row, said once more.
332		ColorIconFile = applyColor(t.IconFile, ColorDim)
333	
334		// An image takes the highlight rather than a third purple: Primary and
335		// Secondary are a mauve and a lavender one notch apart, and the :sec
336		// inventory's first column has exactly two values — the one place where the
337		// two would sit on adjacent rows with nothing else to separate them.
338		ColorIconImage = applyColor(t.IconImage, ColorHighlight)
339	
340		// A disabled shortcut's key (Rule 130), same kind of alias.
341		ColorShortcutDisabled = ColorDim
342	
343		// Rafraîchir les styles qui dépendent des couleurs
344		RefreshStyles()
345	}
